title: Sharing equally
examples: Teacher, what does it mean to share fairly?
If I have ten crayons and share them among four friends, what happens?
Can you show me how to find the leftovers when I share?

explain.say: Today we learn about sharing things fairly with friends. Fair sharing means everyone gets the same amount. Look at this example. We have four red apples to share between two children.
We give one apple to the first child and one apple to the second child. We keep going until all the apples are gone. Each child gets two apples. This is sharing equally.

items: Give one apple to child one
Give one apple to child two

explain.say: Now let us try grouping things. If we have six stickers and we want to make groups of two. We put two stickers together, then another two, and another two. We made three groups.
Sometimes when we share, some things are left over. If we have seven sweets to share between three friends. Everyone gets two sweets. One sweet will be left over for later.

faq.q: What does it mean to share fairly?
faq.a: It means that every person gets the exact same amount of things. If you share five toys between two friends, each friend gets two toys with one left over.
asks: How do I make sure everyone gets the same amount?

faq.q: How do I know how many groups I can make?
faq.a: You count how many items you have and then count how many items you want in each group. For example, ten items in groups of five make two groups.
asks: Can I make groups of four from twelve?

faq.q: What are leftovers when I share?
faq.a: Leftovers are the items that are left after you have shared as much as possible. If you share ten items among three people, two items will be left over.
asks: What is the remainder when sharing?
Why are there extra things left?

faq.q: Can I share things that are not whole numbers?
faq.a: For early years, we usually share whole objects like apples or crayons. Sharing things that are parts is a bit more advanced math.
asks: Can we share a pizza equally?

faq.q: If I share twelve between three, how many does each get?
faq.a: You give one to the first person, one to the second, and one to the third. You keep doing this until all twelve are gone. Each person gets four.
asks: How many in each group of three?

facts: Sharing equally means dividing things into equal parts.
When we group things, we count how many sets we can make.
Leftovers are the items that cannot be shared equally.
If you share ten items among five friends, everyone gets two.

quiz.say: If you have eight pencils to share between four friends, how many does each friend get?
quiz.why: You can give one pencil to each friend, and you will have two pencils left over. Then you give one more to each friend. So each friend gets two pencils.

wrong.1: This is tempting because you might only count the first round of sharing.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you might think you can give three to each friend.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might count the total number of friends.

quiz.say: We have eleven balloons and we want to make groups of three. How many groups can we make?
quiz.why: You put three balloons together, then another three, and then a third group of three. You have two balloons left over.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might add three plus three plus three plus three.
wrong.1: This is tempting because you might just write the total number of balloons.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might only count the first two groups.

quiz.say: If you share twelve cookies among four friends, and you have nothing left, how many cookies did each friend get?
quiz.why: When there are no leftovers, it means the sharing was perfectly equal. Twelve divided by four is three.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might only share half the cookies.
wrong.1: This is tempting because you might think the number of friends is the answer.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you might only give one cookie to each friend.
